set.layering_notes: Sonoma's main local gap source, capitalized by County General Fund, Reinvestment and Revitalization Funds (former RDA), developer in-lieu fees from the residential Affordable Housing Program, non-residential Workforce Housing fees, countywide transient occupancy tax, and loan repayments. Residual receipts loans structured to be compatible with LIHTC investor requirements; interest set by the Commission. Awarded in one annual NOFA together with HOME, CDBG, ESG and LMIHAF so applicants file once. Funds may go to projects inside cities only where the city has a RHNA Sharing Agreement with the County (shelters and congregate facilities exempt). Sponsors must comply with the County Living Wage Ordinance; the policy is silent on prevailing wage, so the Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(E) below-market-loan exemption may apply unless HOME or CDBG is also used. The County does not act as a conduit bond issuer; recent Sonoma deals used CMFA (Burbank Housing $8.12M) and CalHFA. CFH awards are typically $1M to $3M and are counted as local leverage for CTCAC tiebreaker and CDLAC readiness.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: False for the conduit bond financing itself. DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, Public Works Case No. 2006-020, Heber Family Apartments (April 5, 2007), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe, held that privately placed and publicly offered conduit housing revenue bonds are not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b) because the issuer never holds the proceeds or repayments, and that federal LIHTCs are not public funds (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720). The CMFA Esperanza Crossing release states no wage term (https://www.cmfa-ca.com/mercy-housing-preserves-affordable-housing-using-tax-exempt-financing-issued-cmfa/), and a County or city TEFRA approval adds no public funds. Other public sources in the same deal (City or County loans, land, HOME at 12 or more HOME-assisted units, PBVs at 9 or more assisted units) are tested separately and can trigger state or federal prevailing wage.
